questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For my field, I believe "Explore new cultures" counts as academic interest, as i wanted to experience a culture that could seem very similar to what I come from, but actually isn't. I also wanted to go somewhere with possibilities to explore nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I felt welcome, and didn't experience many problems with the university. However, I would have liked to know how different the grading and exams were beforehand, as it was very different from what I am used to in Denmark.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. Also, we got a lot of info in the first days.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an introductory day, where we got to meet other exchange students and learned most of the essential information. Further, we got a lot of mails.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: We had about 7 different places we could apply to, but it seemed like most exchange students were put in two of them. Both were flatshares with 4-6 people living in each

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We had a kitchen in the flatshare

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You have to bring everything yourself, apart from a bed and a small study space. This means you have to buy all kitchen appliances, bed linen and a duvet. That is quite a lot of extra expenses you should expect.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It all happened online. You had sent in some initial wishes before arriving, which you then could change during the first week. You might have to approach some by yourself in order to get the courses you want.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could text a student assistent who would help with all sorts of questions. Most professors also welcomed questions and worries during the first week.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 3 of the 4 i wanted. Then I got the first one i applied for instead.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be quick to apply, and if you really want a certain course, go talk to the teachers or people working at the faculty

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Instead of three years, the undergraduate level is four years. Also, the students are younger than in Denmark. Therefore, in the beginning of the semester, some courses felt really descriptive and less analytical.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I have been used to small discussion classes at UCPH, and at UBC i mostly had larger classes with around 100 people.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Anthropology of Drugs
Vampires, Witches and Zombies: Anthropology of the Supernatural
Ethnography of Special Areas: Medical Anthropology in the Anthropocene
History of Canada: Moments that Matter

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them, if you are interested in the subjects. I would recommend Anthropology of Drugs to everyone, as it helped understand the different laws that affect society in Canada. At the same time, History of Canada helped understand the country i was living in

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Buying everything to be able to live in the apartment: bed linen, duvet and pillow, kitchen supplies.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The food is probably even more expensive than in Denmark, especially cheese. On the other hand, coffee at cafes is cheaper

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were lots of clubs - i attended the Surf Club and the Ski and Boards Club

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Find a club that fits your interests, or something you just want to try. On the first day of school you can meet all the clubs

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
In the summer, go on hikes. You can get a months free All Trails, which helps you find hike trails
In the winter, get a Epic Pass and go skiing in Whistler. If you are a beginner, it might be enough with some of the resorts that's closer, but at least go once to whistler, just to experience the city.
Go watch a sports game - Canucks, Whitecaps or Thunderbirds
Also, the vintage shops are pretty good, and there are loads

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, although I mostly met with other exchange students

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to the people in your class. They might be going to an event afterwards where you can go as well. Also, talk to people in the clubs, they probably know more about the stuff you are already interested in

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any - Canadians find it easier to talk to strangers, which you quickly adapt to

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I liked how friendly people are - they are willing to help and appreciates if you are friendly to them.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Expect to buy loads of stuff for your apartment.
Talk to as many strangers as you can.
Go on trips

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enjoy it :-)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know a culture, and be able to compare to the one at home

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Becoming close friends with other students - four months is a short time

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
